records.subject: Need for a mechanism to combat recurring floods in Assam and other parts in the North Eastern Region.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Kanad Purkyastha:?????????

I seek to draw attention of the Government to the recurring and devastating floods affecting Assam and the entire North Eastern Region. Assam is among India?s most flood-prone States. Nearly 39.58% of its geographical area is flood-prone, almost four times the national average, with an average of 9.31 lakh hectares affected annually.  The recent floods have once again exposed the region?s vulnerability. 99 lives have been lost, while over 1.28 lakh people remain affected across seven districts, despite extensive relief operations. These floods are not caused by rainfall alone. Cloudbursts in upstream areas, trans-boundary river flows, riverbank erosion, siltation, embankment failures and changing climatic patterns aggravate the crisis. I urge the Government to establish a North East Integrated Flood Management Authority to coordinate flood forecasting, river-basin planning and disaster response across the region.

I further urge the Government to: 1. Prepare a Brahmaputra?Barak River Basin Master Plan. 2. Strengthen embankments and undertake scientific river management and dredging. 3. Expand real-time, satellite-and AI-based flood forecasting and early-warning systems. 4. Develop multipurpose reservoirs, retention basins and flood-moderation structures. 5. Build elevated shelters, climate-resilient roads and bridges. 6. Provide long-term assistance for flood-proof housing, crop protection, erosion control and livelihood restoration. The people of Assam and the North East need not merely relief after every flood, but a permanent, scientific and integrated solution.  I urge the Government to treat flood management in the North East as a national priority.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for establishment of a Science Research Institute at Sribhumi, Assam.
Demand for resumption of Air India services from Silchar Airport.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Kanad Purkayastha: I draw attention of the Government regarding the resumption of Air India services to and from Silchar Airport (IXS) in Assam. At present, Silchar Airport is served by only a single private airline. This has led to acute shortage of seats, exorbitant airfares during peak periods, frequent overbooking and serious inconvenience to passengers. Silchar is not merely a district headquarters. It is the principal aviation gateway to the entire Barak Valley, serving three districts of southern Assam and also catering to passengers from Tripura, Mizoram, Manipur and southern Nagaland. With improved infrastructure, expanding educational and medical institutions and rising economic activity, air traffic demand from this region has increased steadily. The absence of Air India services has reduced competition, making connectivity to major metros such as Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Guwahati both difficult and prohibitively expensive. Air India, as the national carrier, has historically played a vital role in connecting remote and strategically important regions of the North-East with the rest of the country. I therefore earnestly urge the Government to consider the early resumption of Air India services to Silchar, or alternatively, the introduction of Air India or Air India Express flights under suitable route rationalization. Such a step will ease passenger hardship, enhance regional connectivity, and advance the Government?s vision of inclusive development of the North-East.

(ENDS)
